text:
Maya: quick sync — spike proposal to split eviction policy out of the residency store and into a stateless "evaluator" service. TL;DR: evaluator makes decisions, emits idempotent directives; residency store becomes the canonical lightweight truth for pins/residency.
Sam: what's the primary motivation? perf or correctness or ops?
Maya: mostly ops/velocity. Want to iterate on eviction algorithms (fairness, hotkey handling) without modifying core residency code. Also reduces blast radius when trying experimental heuristics.
Priya: i'm worried about races — evaluator emits an evict directive while a pin is in-flight. how do we avoid mis-evictions / read-after-write surprises?
Joel: we need ordering guarantees. suggest a monotonic generation counter on residency entries + lease tokens for in-flight ops. directive includes expected gen so stores can reject stale directives.
Maya: proof-of-concept API sketch:
POST /residency/v1/directives
{ "prefix": "tenant:123", "action": "evict", "since_gen": 42, "evaluator_id": "ev-1", "idempotency_key": "ev-1-tenant123-42" }
Sam: and store side logic would apply directive iff current_gen == since_gen (or maybe >= since_gen depending on semantics).
Priya: if we require equality we avoid races, but could leave hot prefixes sticky if things advanced. maybe support a mode: since_gen_match: exact|at_least and default to exact for safety.
Maya: agreed. default safety = exact. we can relax for opportunistic eviction later.
Joel: fallback plan if evaluator unreachable: residency nodes keep conservative behavior (don't evict) and a periodic local compaction can run at higher thresholds. also need quick rollbacks.
Priya: testing matrix: duplicate directives, out-of-order delivery, delayed directives after new pins, and replayed directives. add chaos test that reorders RPCs and injects duplicates.
Sam: backward compatibility: older residency nodes should gracefully ignore unknown fields, but we must gate behavioral change behind a feature flag so we can flip per-cluster.
Maya: metrics to add: directive_apply_latency, directive_reject_count (by reason: gen_mismatch, unknown_prefix), evaluator_emit_rate, evaluator_confidence_score distribution.
Joel: ops: alert when directive_reject_count/gen_mismatch spikes > 0.5% over 5m and when residency_gen_skew > N across nodes. add a runbook: mark feature-flag off, rollback evaluator traffic.
Priya: one more: we need a canonical audit trail for directives for debugging. store directives as append-only metadata on residency entry (bounded retention e.g., 7d).
Maya: decision for spike: implement evaluator service + POST /residency/v1/directives API with exact since_gen matching, idempotency key, append-only directive log on residency, feature flag rollout, and pre-flight chaos tests.
Action items:
- Maya: implement API + evaluator POC + unit tests (owner)
- Sam: residency handler for directives, feature-flag gate, conservative fallback logic (owner)
- Priya: create eval harness + metrics, add directive scenarios to regression evals (owner)
- Joel: add alerts + runbook + canary checklist (owner)
Sam: timeline: 2-week spike for POC + tests, then 1 week for per-cluster canary.
Maya: will open PRs today with design doc + API proto. please review quickly.
